overview: Coroners investigate deaths that are sudden, violent or unexplained. They examine the scene, interview witnesses, order autopsies and complete death certificates that record the cause and manner of death. O*NET rates knowledge of medicine at 4.55 out of 5 for this job and law and government at 4.15. Rules differ by county: some coroners are elected, while medical examiners must be physicians. BLS publishes pay only for the broader compliance officers group, with a median of $80,730. The job involves exposure to disease, outdoor scenes in all weather and constant contact with grieving families.
pay: BLS does not publish pay for coroners alone, so these figures are for the broader compliance officers group. Its median is $80,730, and the top 10% earn $133,720 or more. The District of Columbia has the highest state median at $111,030, 38% above the national figure. Physician medical examiners usually earn far more.

faq.a: BLS reports pay for the broader compliance officers group: a May 2025 median of $80,730. The lowest 10% earn under $48,220 and the top 10% earn $133,720 or more. The District of Columbia, Massachusetts and New Jersey have the highest state medians, all $100,000 or more.

It varies by county. In O*NET data, 35% of coroners hold a bachelor's degree, 15% an associate degree and 15% a post-baccalaureate certificate, while 10% have a high school diploma. Many counties require death investigation training, and medical examiner roles need a medical degree.

faq.q: What does a coroner do every day?
faq.a: A coroner visits death scenes, interviews people present, reviews medical records and arranges autopsies when needed. O*NET rates critical thinking and speaking at 4.12 out of 5 for this job. You also complete death certificates and testify in court, so careful writing matters.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to coroner?
faq.a: The closest are Detectives and Criminal Investigators (88% match), Police Identification and Records Officers (86%) and Forensic Science Technicians (83%), based on O*NET 31.0. Detectives earn a median of $93,790 for their broader BLS group and share the investigative work.
